payload.summary: Highest rung on this ladder is RISKY (8 risky, 10 not proven, 14 proven). That is the strongest concern already listed. It is not a separate check.

report.threatModel: A valid Intel TDX quote proves a TDX-attested registered configuration, not an honest operator. That includes a quote that carries a dstack context. TEE.fail showed that physical access to DDR5 memory can forge TDX quotes, including quotes for dstack contexts. See https://tee.fail/.

live.detail: No live guest endpoint was named. Phala blocks public guest-agent routes by default. Glassbox did not send a nonce. A registration is not a live process. Proven at registration only.

anchor.reason: Report hash anchoring is off. Glassbox does not send a transaction. Report sha256: c69e80dae96228f97248c3d3efde28249ddeb4ee2b03de79c4452297cf526571. A later opt-in can publish this sha256 on NEAR. No NEAR key is loaded, and no account is required today.

findings.title: Registered configuration matches a vulnerable configuration
findings.plainEnglish: Heuristic. The registered configuration references /var/run/tappd.sock and has no os-image-hash event. The event log has a rootfs-hash event and no os-image-hash event. That pattern fits dstack before 0.5 (often described as 0.3.x or 0.4.x). It matches a vulnerable configuration in the 0.3.1–0.6.0 range. It does not identify an exact release. The fixed releases named by Phala are 0.6.1 and 0.5.12.

findings.title: Registered configuration names secret-looking env vars
findings.plainEnglish: These env names match a secret-looking pattern: NEAR_SEED_PHRASE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. Glassbox reports the names only. A name in the registered configuration is not proof of the value, and the value is not shown.

provenance.label: Local check of the supplied file. Not a live chain observation.

findings.title: 20 Nov 2026 auto-upgrade or v0.3.x retirement may apply
findings.plainEnglish: Phala's 19 Oct 2026 post-mortem says to move to v0.6.1 or v0.5.12 by 19 Nov 2026. From 20 Nov 2026, remaining v0.5.x and v0.6.0 CVMs are auto-upgraded in batches (24 hour notice on the status page), and v0.3.x is retired with no upgrade path (enterprise excluded). Shade v1 approves an app codehash, so an OS image change does not by itself invalidate that codehash. A v0.3.x-era registration can still be retired by the operator. This registered configuration only matches a pre-0.5 pattern, so Glassbox cannot tell a v0.3.x retirement apart from another unfixed build.

limitations: Findings that cite a quote or an app compose describe the registered configuration. They do not establish what the account is executing now.
A valid TDX quote proves a TDX-attested registered configuration. It does not prove an honest operator. See the threat-model paragraph.
Glassbox does not judge payment correctness, and it has no payment or send step. That is Gideon (https://github.com/Adelekejr/Gideon-near), a separate NEAR pre-send checker by the same builder.
Comparisons with Shade's 0.5.7/0.5.8 table use that project's published measurements. Heuristics are marked on the finding.
This report was built from a file or pasted JSON. A PROVEN row compares values in that input, or verifies a quote carried in it. It is not a fresh chain read.
sources: @phala/dcap-qvl 0.7.1 (Apache-2.0) for TDX quote verification. QE identity is mandatory. TCB status is enforced. PCCS allowlist: https://pccs.phala.network, https://api.trustedservices.intel.com, https://certificates.trustedservices.intel.com.
Input: local JSON. Chain history was not queried.
Shade measurement tables: shade-agent-cli (Apache-2.0), dstack 0.5.7 and 0.5.8 only.
